name: AD7616BSTZ
title: AD7616: 16-channel data acquisition system, dual simultaneous-sampling 16-bit SAR ADC, ±10 V/±5 V/±2.5 V bipolar inputs, 80-lead LQFP
summary: A 16-channel data acquisition chip built round two 16-bit SAR converters that sample a pair of channels at once, up to 1 MSPS per pair. Each of the 16 single-ended inputs takes ±10 V, ±5 V or ±2.5 V from one 5 V supply, presenting a fixed 1 MΩ with clamps good to ±21 V and a first-order antialiasing filter, so no driver amplifier is needed. A 2.5 V reference, averaging filter (OSR up to 128), 32-step sequencer with burst mode, CRC and either a 16-bit parallel or SPI-type serial port are on chip; it is set up by pins (hardware mode) or by registers (software mode).
key_figures: ±10 V, ±5 V, ±2.5 V, per channel in software mode
90.5 dB typ, ±10 V, no oversampling; 92 dB at OSR = 2
±1 LSB typ, ±2 LSB max / ±0.99 LSB max
2.5 V internal or external, 2.495 V to 2.505 V

circuits.description: The ADC with its supply, regulator and reference capacitors and one input channel on each ADC. 5 V on VCC and the host's 2.5 V or 3.3 V on VDRIVE are each bypassed with 10 µF and 0.1 µF. The two internal LDO outputs each get 10 µF to their own ground pins, REFINOUT gets 0.1 µF X8R and REFCAP 10 µF X5R. Each input reaches the chip through equal resistors R in the signal and its ground return, with a capacitor C across the pair at the pins; every other channel is wired the same way.
notes: Every channel x takes the same R, R and C on VxA/VxAGND and VxB/VxBGND as channel 0.
All four VCC pins are on the 5V net.

operation.text: Two 16-bit charge-redistribution SAR converters sample at the same instant, each fed through a multiplexer from its own eight channels (V0A to V7A for ADC A, V0B to V7B for ADC B) and the diagnostic inputs. Every input passes a clamp, a 1 MΩ scaling stage and a first-order low-pass before the multiplexer; a 2.5 V band gap, a reference buffer to 4.096 V, an optional averaging filter, a sequencer and parallel and serial ports complete the chip. It runs from one 5 V supply.

At the end of a full reset the HW_RNGSELx pins pick the mode: 00 gives software mode, configured through registers over either interface; any other code gives hardware mode, configured only by pins, with the code also setting the range of all 16 inputs. Registers cannot be reached in hardware mode. Leaving a mode takes another full reset.

In hardware mode a channel is always converted together with its namesake on the other ADC (V0A with V0B, and so on). In software mode any A channel can be paired with any B channel or a diagnostic channel. Diagnostic channels need software mode.

Each input accepts true bipolar single-ended signals of ±10 V, ±5 V or ±2.5 V. In software mode each channel has its own range from the input range registers. In hardware mode a change on HW_RNGSELx acts at once, but the input then needs about 120 µs to settle on top of the normal acquisition time, so wiring the pins fixed is the usual choice.
The input impedance is a fixed 1 MΩ, independent of sampling rate, so a sensor or source can be connected directly with no driver amplifier and no bipolar supplies.

Clamps on each input carry no current between −20 V and +20 V and conduct beyond that. A series resistor should hold the clamp current to ±10 mA for inputs past ±20 V. Any resistance in series with VxA or VxB must be matched by the same resistance in the VxAGND or VxBGND line, otherwise the mismatch shows up as an offset and gain error on that channel. The clamps are for transient overvoltage; leaving them conducting for long periods, powered or not, is not advised.
A first-order Butterworth low-pass sits on every input; its corner is typically 39 kHz on the ±10 V range and 33 kHz on the ±5 V range.

Output is twos complement. Code transitions fall at 1/2 LSB and 3/2 LSB and so on; one LSB is the full-scale span divided by 65,536: 305 µV on ±10 V, 152 µV on ±5 V and 76 µV on ±2.5 V. The first transition is at −FS + 1/2 LSB, midscale at 0 V − 1/2 LSB and the last at +FS − 3/2 LSB.

REFSEL, read at the end of a full reset, chooses the reference: high enables the internal 2.5 V band gap, which also appears on REFINOUT; low disables it and an external 2.5 V must drive REFINOUT, which is then high impedance. Either 2.5 V is amplified by an always-on buffer to about 4.096 V on REFCAP, the voltage the SAR converters use. REFINOUT needs 100 nF X8R to REFINOUTGND; REFCAP needs 10 µF X5R to REFGND. An external reference goes in through a 10 kΩ series resistor. The internal reference must be buffered before any other circuit uses it.

Holding RESET low longer than 1.2 µs puts the part in shutdown, where everything is off and all registers go back to their defaults; supply current is typically 78 µA. Raising RESET returns to normal mode: a register write is possible after about 240 µs and a conversion after 15 ms.

An optional first-order sinc filter averages 2 to 128 samples per channel (OS2 to OS0 pins in hardware serial mode, read at full reset; OS bits in software mode, applying to all channels) and decimates the result to 16 bits. The first sample is taken on the CONVST edge, the rest on an internal clock. Higher ratios raise SNR, lower the −3 dB bandwidth and the usable sample rate, and stretch BUSY; acquisition and conversion time grow in proportion to the ratio. With the sequencer or burst mode, all samples of one channel are taken before moving on.

VCC powers the analog circuits and VDRIVE the digital interface; each wants 10 µF in parallel with 100 nF, the small capacitor nearest the pin. Internal LDOs make 1.87 V (ALDO, on REGCAP) and 1.89 V (DLDO, on REGCAPD), each decoupled by its own 10 µF to its ground pin. Supply sequencing is not critical; VDRIVE first and then VCC is preferred, with RESET held low until both are steady.

A full reset (RESET low at least 1.2 µs) restores the power-on state; 15 ms after release the part is configured and can convert. On release the levels of HW_RNGSELx, REFSEL, SER/PAR and DB4/SER1W set mode, reference and interface; in hardware mode CRCEN, BURST, SEQEN and OSx are latched too. These stay fixed until the next full reset. A partial reset (40 ns to 500 ns low) restarts the sequencer, digital filter, SPI and both SARs, drops the conversion in progress and keeps register contents and latched settings; 50 ns after release the part can convert. Software mode needs one dummy conversion after a partial reset. In hardware mode CHSELx and HW_RNGSELx are read on release of either reset to set the first channel pair, the sequencer start and the range.

CHSELx pick the channel pair. Their level when a reset ends sets the first pair; after that they are read while BUSY is high to set the pair for the following conversion, so they must be set before the CONVST rising edge and held until BUSY falls.
The channel register picks the pair for the next conversion; after power-up or reset V0A and V0B are selected.

SER/PAR low. After BUSY falls, CS and RD together put a result on DB15 to DB0: the first RD falling edge gives the ADC A result, the next the ADC B result. At least two reads per conversion; CRC, status and burst add more. CS rising three-states the bus, which lets several devices share it. A register write is one 16-bit word on the bus with D15 = 1, address in D14:D9 and data in D8:D0, latched on the WR rising edge. A register read writes D15 = 0 with the address, then a normal read returns the contents.

SER/PAR high. CS falling enables SDOA and SDOB and presents the MSB; each SCLK rising edge shifts out the next bit. In 2-wire mode (SER1W high) ADC A results come on SDOA and ADC B on SDOB, 16 clocks per conversion; this is needed for full throughput. In 1-wire mode (SER1W low) both results come on SDOA, A then B, in 32 clocks framed by one CS or two, and SDOB is left open. Hold CS low across longer frames (status word, burst). Register writes are 16-bit words on SDI with D15 = 1; a read command (D15 = 0) returns the register on the next frame, which may carry another command or a NOP. Reachable SPI clock depends on VDRIVE and SDO load.

Hardware mode: SEQEN high at full reset enables a sequential sequencer that always starts at V0A/V0B and runs to the pair set by CHSELx; to change the end channel, set CHSELx during the last BUSY pulse of the running sequence. Software mode: a 32-layer stack, each layer pairing any A input with any B input or a diagnostic channel; depth 1 to 32 is set by the SSRENx bit of the last layer. Setup: set ranges, load the stack, set SSRENx on the last layer, set SEQEN in the configuration register, give one dummy CONVST, then convert and read through the stack; it wraps to the first layer. A partial reset moves the pointer back to layer one and keeps the stack.

With burst on, one CONVST edge converts every step of the sequence; BUSY stays high until all are done and results then come out in sequence order. Hardware mode: BURST and SEQEN both high at full reset, the length set by CHSELx (change it during the next BUSY pulse). Software mode: set BURSTEN together with SEQEN. Throughput falls with sequence length (burst time equation).
Software mode can convert VCC and the ALDO voltage through the channel register or the stack. Readings are accurate only below 250 kSPS.
Selecting the self test code in the channel register forces fixed results: 0xAAAA from ADC A and 0x5555 from ADC B.

An optional 8-bit CRC is available in software mode (either interface) and hardware serial mode, not in hardware parallel mode. Hardware mode: CRCEN high at full reset. Software mode: CRCEN or STATUSEN bit. When on, a 16-bit status word follows the results: the channel IDs of the last pair in the upper byte and the CRC in the lower byte. The CRC starts at zero and runs over A then B of each pair in turn. Hamming distance is 4 for up to 119 bits of results and 1 above that.

crc_out(data, crc), with data the 16-bit result and crc the running 8-bit value: crc_out[0] = d14^d12^d8^d7^d6^d0^c0^c4^c6; crc_out[1] = d15^d14^d13^d12^d9^d6^d1^d0^c1^c4^c5^c6^c7; crc_out[2] = d15^d13^d12^d10^d8^d6^d2^d1^d0^c0^c2^c4^c5^c7; crc_out[3] = d14^d13^d11^d9^d7^d3^d2^d1^c1^c3^c5^c6; crc_out[4] = d15^d14^d12^d10^d8^d4^d3^d2^c0^c2^c4^c6^c7; crc_out[5] = d15^d13^d11^d9^d5^d4^d3^c1^c3^c5^c7; crc_out[6] = d14^d12^d10^d6^d5^d4^c2^c4^c6; crc_out[7] = d15^d13^d11^d7^d6^d5^c3^c5^c7. For each pair n: crc1 = crc_out(An, crc); crc = crc_out(Bn, crc1).

Software mode has six read/write registers (configuration, channel, four input range), 32 sequencer stack registers and a read-only status register. The top seven bits of each 16-bit word are W/R and REGADDR[5:0]; the low nine bits are data.
80-lead LQFP, 14 mm square body, 0.65 mm lead pitch, JEDEC MS-026-BEC.
